541	Run `uip is connections --help` or `uip is resources --help` for all options.
542	
543	---
544	
545	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
546	
547	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
548	
549	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
550	
551	### How connector nodes reference bindings
552	
553	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
554	
555	```json
556	"context": [
557	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
558	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
559	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
560	]
561	```
562	
563	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
564	
565	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
566	
567	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
568	
569	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
570	
571	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
572	
573	```json
574	"bindings": [
575	  {
576	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
577	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
578	    "type": "string",
579	    "resource": "Connection",
580	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
581	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
582	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
583	  },
584	  {
585	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
586	    "name": "FolderKey",
587	    "type": "string",
588	    "resource": "Connection",
589	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
590	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
591	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
592	  }
593	]
594	```
595	
596	| Field | Value |
597	|-------|-------|
598	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
599	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
600	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
601	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
602	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
603	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
604	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
605	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
606	
607	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and writes the two top-level `bindings[]` entries — claiming the empty `ConnectionId` stub that `node add` hoisted (matched by name) and adding the `FolderKey` row. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
608	
609	> **An empty-keyed Connection binding is a defect, not a cosmetic nit.** A `bindings[]` row with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"`, and `resourceKey: ""` faults Studio Web at runtime with `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'Connection')`. `node add` hoists exactly one such stub (`name: "<connector-key> connection"`); `node configure` **claims it in place** (matching by that name), so a fully configured connector leaves no empty row — do not expect a "duplicate" empty pair, and never hand-edit `bindings[]` to remove one (it is CLI-owned). The only legitimate empty stub is the No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration case above, where the node is deliberately left unconfigured and the flow is known not to pass `flow validate` yet. An empty stub that survives a real `node configure` — or lingers after a connector node is removed — is a CLI bug to report, not something to paper over by hand.
610	
611	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.
612	
613	### Single-connector example (Jira)
614	
615	```json
616	"bindings": [
617	  {
618	    "id": "bJiraConn",
619	    "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",
620	    "type": "string",
621	    "resource": "Connection",
622	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
623	    "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
624	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
625	  },
626	  {
627	    "id": "bJiraFolder",
628	    "name": "FolderKey",
629	    "type": "string",
630	    "resource": "Connection",
631	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
632	    "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
633	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
634	  }
635	]
636	```
637	
638	### Multi-connector example (Jira + Slack)
639	
640	Two unique connections → four entries in `bindings[]` (two per connection):
641	
642	```json
643	"bindings": [
644	  { "id": "bJiraConn",   "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",   "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
645	  { "id": "bJiraFolder", "name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "folder-uuid-for-jira",                "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" },
646	  { "id": "bSlackConn",  "name": "uipath-salesforce-slack connection", "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
647	  { "id": "bSlackFolder","name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "folder-uuid-for-slack",               "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" }
648	]
649	```
650	
651	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
652	
653	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
654	
655	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
656	
657	```json
658	{
659	  "version": "2.0",
660	  "resources": [
661	    {
662	      "resource": "Connection",
663	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
664	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
665	      "value": {
666	        "ConnectionId": {
667	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
668	          "isExpression": false,
669	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
670	        }
671	      },
672	      "metadata": {
673	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",
674	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
675	        "DisplayLabel": "my-jira-connection",
676	        "UseConnectionService": "true",
677	        "Connector": "uipath-atlassian-jira"
678	      }
679	    }
680	  ]
681	}
682	```
683	
684	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
685	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
686	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.
687	
688	### Other binding resource types (triggers, queues, scheduled)
689	
690	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.
691	
692	| Generated `bindings_v2.json` resource | Authored via | Key source fields |
693	|---------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|
694	| `Connection` | Top-level `bindings[]` with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"` | Covered above |
695	| `EventTrigger` | Top-level `bindings[]` + the trigger node itself | See connector-trigger plugin |
696	| `Property` | Trigger node's `model.inputs.filterFields` | See connector-trigger plugin |
697	| `Queue` / `TimeTrigger` | Specific trigger types | See relevant trigger plugin |
698	
699	> **Never hardcode connection IDs.** Always fetch them from IS at authoring time. Connection IDs are tenant-specific and change across environments.
700	
701	---
702	
703	## Debug
704	
705	### Common Errors
706	
707	| Error | Cause | Fix |
708	| --- | --- | --- |
709	| No connection found | Connection not bound — top-level `bindings[]` missing or `resourceKey` doesn't match the node | Run Step 1 above to bind a connection; verify both entries (`ConnectionId` + `FolderKey`) are in the top-level `bindings[]` |
710	| Connection ping failed | Connection expired or misconfigured | Re-authenticate the connection in the IS portal |
711	| Missing `inputs.detail` | Node added but not configured | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with the detail JSON (Step 6) |
712	| Reference field has display name instead of ID | `uip is resources run list` was skipped | Resolve the reference field to get the actual ID (Step 4) |
713	| Node faults at runtime with "resource not found" or similar after a clean build and validate | Reference field uses an ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a Slack channel ID from workspace A pasted into a node bound to workspace B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 4 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
714	| Required field missing at runtime | Required input field not provided | Check metadataFile for all `required: true` fields in both `requestFields` and `parameters` |
715	| `$vars` expression unresolvable | Node outputs block missing or node not connected | Verify the node has edges and upstream outputs are correctly referenced |
716	| `connectorMethodInfo` missing method/path | Used `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id` for enriched metadata (Step 2) |
717	| `bindings_v2.json` malformed or stale | It was hand-edited (the CLI overwrites edits on next debug/pack), or top-level `bindings[]` was mutated by hand | Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly. Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` on the affected connector node(s) so the CLI re-emits top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from those at the next debug/pack. Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |
718	| Connector key not found | Wrong key name | Run `uip is connectors list --output json` — keys are often prefixed with `uipath-` |
719	| FilterBuilder UI shows `undefined` when activity is reopened in Studio Web; flow runs at debug | A raw `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` string was passed instead of a structured filter tree, so `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>` is empty. The runtime side works but Studio Web has no tree to render. | Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` with `--detail '{"filter": {...tree...}}'` — the CLI populates both halves. See Step 6a above and [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql). |
720	| `node configure` fails with `'<name>' is a FilterBuilder parameter — pass a structured filter tree under --detail.filter` | Same root cause — raw string under `queryParameters` for a FilterBuilder param | Move the value into `--detail.filter` as a structured tree. The CLI catches this at configure time so it never reaches Studio Web. |
721	| Data Service query returns every record (or faults with malformed CEQL ending in `AND`) though a filter tree was configured; `node configure` reported Success | A filter-tree leaf's field id did not match the entity schema (matching is case-sensitive). The compiler drops unmatched leaves without an error — one bad leaf empties the query string, a bad leaf beside a good one leaves a dangling `AND`. | Compare the tree's field ids against the entity schema — `uip df entities list --output json` for the entity `Id`, then `uip df entities get <entity-id> --output json` for the field names. Re-run `node configure` with the exact ids. See Step 6a. |
722	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Expected a field name expression but got 'StringValue'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL string (e.g. Data Service `queryExpression`) quotes the **field name**: `'accountNumber' = '...'`. CEQL reads a quoted token as a string literal. Only `node configure --detail.filter` builds the expression for you; a string hand-written into the `.flow` JSON reaches IS unchecked. | Field names bare, only values quoted: `` `accountNumber = '${$vars...}'` ``. Or author via `--detail.filter` so the CLI compiles the CEQL. |
723	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Unsupported value expression 'Column' on field '<field>'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL double-quotes the **value**, typically from a concatenation with escaped quotes: `` =js:"accountNumber = \"" + String(v) + "\"" ``. CEQL reads a double-quoted token as a column reference, not a string literal. | Single-quote the value inside the concatenation: `` =js:"accountNumber = '" + String($vars.<node>.output.<field>) + "'" ``. Or author via `--detail.filter`. See [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
724	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request` and the filter uses `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, or `le` | OData aliases in a hand-authored CEQL string. CEQL accepts only symbol operators. | Replace with `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`. See the alias table in [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
725	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues must be an array of [key, value] tuples, not an object map` | Wrote `parameterValues: {key: value}` (object map). Studio Web emits its `Map<string,string\|null>` as `Array.from(entries())` — tuples, not object | Convert to tuples: `[["key", "value"], ...]`. See Step 6c. |
726	| Custom fields fault at runtime with token unresolved | A `{token}` in `objectActions[].apiConfiguration.url` or `body` has no entry in `parameterValues` | Re-read the ObjectAction's `apiConfiguration` placeholders, add the missing tuple to `parameterValues`. CLI does not validate token coverage. |
727	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails has unknown keys: ObjectActionName, ParameterValues` | PascalCase inner keys instead of camelCase | Use `objectActionName` / `parameterValues`. Studio Web emits camelCase; PascalCase is rejected. |
728	| Field rejected at runtime as unknown (e.g. `"unknown field 'fields.labels[*]'"`) after a clean `flow validate` | `[*]` was left in the `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key. `[*]` is an array marker from `requestFields[].name`, not part of the wire key. | Strip `[*]` from the key in your `--detail` payload, pass a `=js:` expression returning the array, and re-run `node configure`. Fields with `[*].` (segments after the `[*]`) are not authorable. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
729	| Array field round-trips empty after a clean `flow validate` | Literal JSON array authored for a `[*]` field — validates but does not bind | Author as `=js:` expression returning the array: `"users": "=js:(['U123ABC', 'U456DEF'])"`. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
730	
731	### Debug Tips
732	
733	1. **Always check top-level `bindings[]` in the `.flow` file** — connector nodes silently fail if a binding is missing or malformed. Compare against the CLI-emitted `bindings[]` shape documented above (§ Top-level `bindings[]` shape). Do not inspect `bindings_v2.json` as ground truth; it is regenerated from the `.flow` on every debug/pack.
734	2. **Compare inputs against metadataFile** — the full metadata (from `is resources describe`) has every field with types, descriptions, and whether it's required
735	3. **`flow validate` does NOT catch connector-specific issues** — validation only checks JSON schema and graph structure. Missing `inputs.detail` fields, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime (`flow debug`)
736	4. **If a connector key doesn't work** — list all connectors: `uip is connectors list --output json`. Keys are often prefixed with `uipath-`
737	5. **Query/path parameters** — some required parameters appear only in the metadataFile `parameters` section, not in `requestFields`. Check both.
738	6. **`node configure` populates bindings automatically** — it appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries and populates `inputs.detail`. The generated `bindings_v2.json` follows from these at debug/pack time. If you cannot run `node configure` (no live tenant, sandbox forbids it, planning-only request), record the planned binding entries in the sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` per the No-Live-Tenant flow above — do not author `bindings[]` directly on the `.flow` as a substitute, and note that the flow will not pass `flow validate` until a real `node configure` runs.

1	# Resources
2	
3	Resources represent the data objects available through a connector (e.g., Salesforce Account, Contact, Opportunity). Each resource supports a set of CRUD operations.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	## Contents
8	- Listing and Describing Resources
9	- Response Fields
10	- Describe Response
11	- Describe Failures
12	- Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
13	- Execute Operations
14	- Pagination
15	- Execute Error Handling
16	
17	For reference field resolution (simple refs, dependency chains, required field validation), see [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md).
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Listing and Describing Resources
22	
23	**Always pass `--connection-id`** to get connection-specific metadata including custom objects and fields. Without it, only standard objects/fields are returned.
24	
25	## Response Fields
26	
27	| Field | Description |
28	|---|---|
29	| **`Name`** | Resource identifier (used in commands) |
30	| `DisplayName` | Human-readable name |
31	| `Path` | API path for this resource |
32	| `Type` | Resource type (standard, custom) |
33	| `SubType` | Sub-type (e.g., method, entity) |
34	
35	## Describe Response
36	
37	The describe command returns metadata from the raw API. The output depends on whether `--operation` is provided.
38	
39	### Without `--operation` — operation summary
40	
41	Returns which operations the resource supports:
42	
43	| Field | Description |
44	|---|---|
45	| **`availableOperations`** | List of operations — each with `method` (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE), `name` (Create/List/etc.), `description`, `curated` (display name) |
46	| **`hint`** | Instructs to use `--operation` for field details |
47	
48	### With `--operation` — per-operation field detail
49	
50	Returns the full field breakdown for the specified operation:
51	
52	| Field | Description |
53	|---|---|
54	| **`operation`** | Operation info — `method`, `name`, `description`, `path`, `curated` display name |
55	| **`parameters`** | Path and query parameters (NOT body fields) — each with `name`, `type` (path/query), `dataType`, `required`, `defaultValue`, `reference` |
56	| **`requestFields`** | Fields to send in `--body` — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName`, `required`, `description`, `reference`, `enum` |
57	| **`responseFields`** | Fields returned in the response — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName` |
58	
59	> **Always use `--operation`** to get actionable field detail. Without it you only see which operations exist.
60	
61	### Key field properties
62	
63	- **`required: true`** — field must be provided in `--body` or `--query`. Do NOT skip.
64	- **`reference`** — field value must be looked up from another resource. See [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md). When baking a static value for a reference field, also emit `designTimeMetadata.designTimeLookups` so the edit-UI renders a label — see [reference-resolution.md — Static Reference-Value Labeling](reference-resolution.md#static-reference-value-labeling).
65	- **`enum`** — field only accepts the listed values (e.g., `["low", "normal", "high"]`).
66	
67	Results are cached locally. Use `--refresh` to bypass cache after re-auth or schema changes.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Describe Failures
72	
73	Some resources return an error on describe. This is a **server-side metadata gap** — do not retry with `--refresh`.
74	
75	**Recovery:**
76	
77	1. **Skip describe entirely** — do not waste calls retrying.
78	2. **Infer fields from user context** — use the field names and values the user provided in their request.
79	3. **Infer reference fields from naming** — see [reference-resolution.md — Inferring References Without Describe](reference-resolution.md#inferring-references-without-describe).
80	4. **Attempt execute directly** — let the server validate. If a field is rejected, read the error and adjust.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
85	
86	For connectors whose required fields depend on parent-field selections (Jira `GenerateSchema` keyed off project + issue type, Salesforce SOQL `GenerateQuerySchema` keyed off the query string, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant` keyed off `tenantEntityName`), the base `describe` returns only base fields. To preview the full required-field set the runtime will see, pass parent values via `-f, --field`:
87	
88	```bash
89	# Jira: project + issue type → custom fields (GET, query-param tokens)
90	uip is resources describe uipath-atlassian-jira curated_create_issue \
91	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
92	  -f fields.project.key=ENGCE \
93	  -f fields.issuetype.id=3 \
94	  --output json
95	
96	# Salesforce SOQL: query string → response columns (POST, body token)
97	uip is resources describe uipath-salesforce-sfdc query_records \
98	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
99	  -f query="SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Status = 'Active'" \
100	  --output json
101	```
102	
103	What it does — runs the matching api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service (same path Studio Web's dispatcher uses), then merges the response into `requestFields` per the action's `onSuccess.remapConfiguration`. Use it before validating required fields to catch project- or operation-specific mandatory fields the base describe can't see.
104	
105	| Flag | Notes |
106	|------|-------|
107	| `-f, --field <name=value>` | Repeatable. Token names match `apiConfiguration.url` and `apiConfiguration.body` placeholders verbatim — no `_sub_` encoding (encoding only applies when caching parent values for runtime replay; see [activities.md — Custom Fields](activities.md#custom-fields-objectactionsactiontypeapi)). |
108	| `--action <name>` | Optional. Disambiguates when more than one api-type action could match the field set. |
109	
110	Requires `--connection-id` and `--operation`. Cache is bypassed when `--field` is supplied — the action response varies per parent-field combination. The merge mode (`replace` / `append` / `prepend` / `noop`) comes from the action's `remapConfiguration.input`; for Jira `GenerateSchema` it is `replace`.
111	
112	When no api-type action's `rules[]` are satisfied by the supplied fields, the CLI errors with `No api-type ObjectAction matched for fields [...]`. List the operation's actions from the describe output's `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (or top-level `objectActions[]` for older shapes) to see which fields each action requires.
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Execute Operations
117	
118	| Verb | Description | `--body` | `--query` |
119	|---|---|---|---|
120	| `create` | Create a new record | Yes | No |
121	| `list` | Retrieve multiple records | No | Optional (`limit=10&offset=0`) |
122	| `get` | Get a single record by ID | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
123	| `update` | Partial update (PATCH) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
124	| `delete` | Delete a record | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
125	| `replace` | Full replacement (PUT) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
126	
127	> **Update** (PATCH) = change specific fields. **Replace** (PUT) = overwrite entire record. Default to **Update** unless the user says "replace" or "overwrite".
128	
129	### Filtering Results with `--output-filter`
130	
131	Use the global `--output-filter` flag with a JMESPath expression to extract specific fields from large responses if possible via JMESPath.
132	
133	```bash
134	# Extract only id, name, and email from a user list
135	uip is resources run list "<CONNECTOR_KEY>" "<OBJECT_NAME>" \
136	  --connection-id "<CONNECTION_ID>" \
137	  --output json \
138	  --output-filter "Data[].{id: id, name: name, email: profile.email}"
139	```
140	
141	Common JMESPath patterns:
142	
143	| Pattern | Effect |
144	|---|---|
145	| `Data[]` | Return all records (unwrap the Data envelope) |
146	| `Data[].name` | Return just the `name` field from each record |
147	| `Data[].{id: id, name: name}` | Return selected fields as objects |
148	| `Data[?status=='active']` | Filter records by field value |
149	| `Data[0]` | Return only the first record |
150	
151	---
152	
153	## Pagination
154	
155	`uip is resources run list` may not return all results in a single call. **Always check for pagination** when searching for a specific item or listing all items.
156	
157	### Pagination rules
158	
159	1. **Always check `Data.Pagination`** — every `list` response may contain pagination state. Never assume a single page contains all results.
160	2. **Complete the pagination loop** — when searching for a specific item, keep paginating until `Data.Pagination.HasMore` is `"false"` or the item is found. Do NOT abandon pagination mid-loop to try alternative APIs (e.g., search endpoints, admin endpoints, HTTP fallback).
161	3. **Stop early on match** — if you find the target item in the current page, stop. No need to fetch remaining pages.
162	4. **Report not-found only after exhausting all pages** — only conclude an item does not exist after `HasMore` is `"false"` and every page has been checked.
163	
164	### Connector pagination
165	
166	Most IS connectors use the `elements-*` pagination protocol. The CLI returns pagination state nested inside `Data.Pagination`:
167	
168	- **`Data.Pagination.HasMore`**: `"true"` or `"false"` — indicates if more pages exist
169	- **`Data.Pagination.NextPageToken`**: the token value to use for the next page
170	
171	**IMPORTANT:** The query parameter name is `nextPage` (NOT `nextPageToken`). Pass the value from `Data.Pagination.NextPageToken` as `--query "nextPage=<value>"`.
172	
173	```bash
174	# First page (do not pass pageSize unless the user explicitly requests a specific page size)
175	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
176	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
177	# → Check Data.Pagination.HasMore and Data.Pagination.NextPageToken in the JSON response
178	
179	# Subsequent pages — use nextPage as the query param name (NOT nextPageToken)
180	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
181	  --connection-id "<id>" --query "nextPage=<value-from-NextPageToken>" --output json
182	# → Continue until Data.Pagination.HasMore is "false" or target item is found
183	```
184	
185	Example response:
186	```json
187	{
188	  "Result": "Success",
189	  "Code": "ExecuteOperation",
190	  "Data": {
191	    "items": [ ... ],
192	    "Pagination": {
193	      "HasMore": "true",
194	      "NextPageToken": "eyJwYWdl..."
195	    }
196	  }
197	}
198	```
199	
200	### Anti-patterns
201	
202	- **Do NOT check `Data.nextPage`** — pagination lives at `Data.Pagination.HasMore` and `Data.Pagination.NextPageToken`, not at `Data.nextPage`.
203	- **Do NOT abandon pagination to try other APIs** — if you are paginating through `conversations` to find a channel, do not stop mid-loop to call `admin_conversations_search`, `search_all`, or `search_messages`. Complete the loop first.
204	- **Do NOT conclude "not found" after one page** — a single page may return only a fraction of the total results. Always check `Data.Pagination.HasMore` before concluding.
205	
206	### Query-param pagination (offset/limit)
207	
208	Some resources support `offset`/`limit` via `--query`:
209	
210	```bash
211	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<object>" \
212	  --connection-id "<id>" --query "limit=50&offset=0" --output json
213	# → next page: --query "limit=50&offset=50"
214	```
215	
216	Stop when the result set is empty or smaller than the limit.
217	
218	### HTTP connector exception
219	
220	Connectors with key `uipath-uipath-http` do NOT use the `elements-*` pagination headers. These depend on vendor-specific pagination. Handle on a case-by-case basis.
221	
222	---
223	
224	## Execute Error Handling
225	
226	When an execute command fails, the CLI returns:
227	- **`Message`**: HTTP status (e.g., `400 Bad Request`)
228	- **`Instructions`**: The raw vendor error response body as JSON
229	
230	### How to diagnose failures
231	
232	1. **Read `Message`** — the HTTP status code tells you the category (400 = bad request, 403 = forbidden, 404 = not found, etc.)
233	2. **Read `Instructions`** — the raw vendor error body tells you WHAT specifically failed (invalid field, missing required value, permission denied, etc.)
234	3. **Use discovery to fix** — run `describe` to get valid field names, run `list` to get valid values for reference fields
235	4. **Retry with fixes** — apply the specific correction and re-execute (max 2 retries)
236	
237	For the full recovery loop, see [agent-workflow.md — Error Recovery](agent-workflow.md#error-recovery).

commands.result_summary: 1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order.
